## Meaningfully reducing MAP consumption is hard

::::: columns
::: {.column width="62%"}
![](images/appetite-meta.png){width="100%"}
:::

::: {.column width="38%"}
- My firs project was a [Meta-analytic review](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.appet.2025.108233) of meat and animal product (MAP) reduction interventions
- "But what do the good studies say??" was our question, which meant only RCTs, $\geq$ 25 per arm, direct consumption measure, & $\geq$ 1 day follow-up
- This winnows thousands of papers down to 35 (41 studies and 112 interventions)
:::
:::::

## What was tried?

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{images/appetite-main-results.png}

\small SMD = standardized mean difference
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
Main approaches:

- **Persuasion**: animal welfare, environment, health
- **Choice architecture**: nudges, defaults
- **Psychology**: mostly norms experiments

**Overall: small, sparse effects** — generally changes of a few percentage points. Sad!
:::
:::::

## Movement leaders reached the same conclusion

::::: columns
::: {.column width="28%"}
![](images/MEAT.jpg){width="100%"}
:::

::: {.column width="72%"}
- Around the same time, movement orgs (as far as I can tell) concluded persuasion wasn't working and shifted to
  - **Defaults**: plant-forward menus at scale (e.g., universities, hospitals)
  - **Alt proteins**: Bruce Friedrich and the Good Food Institute
  - **Corporate & political campaigns**: cage-free & BCC commitments, gestation crate bans
:::
:::::

## Defaults: sorry, I'm a skeptic

- No defaults study met our inclusion criteria :(
- No evidence either way on [regression to the meat](https://regressiontothemeat.substack.com/) (rebound at the next meal)
- One post-pub study ([Ginn & Sparkman 2024](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0272494423002748)) met our criteria and found + results. but also noncompliance at one school, lower sales on default days, and no measures of spatial spillovers (what people who leave the default station do instead). So net effects on meat are a bit of guesswork (not a knock on the study!)
- Prior: things don't scale up. Especially [nduges](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.3982/ECTA18709) but really things in general: [site selection bias](https://academic.oup.com/qje/article-abstract/130/3/1117/1933105?login=false), less [skilled/motivated administrators](https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.p20171115) at scale. [publication bias](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2200300119), & [compensating behavior in the long-run](https://www.bu.edu/bulawreview/files/2023/12/STEVENSON.pdf)

## Meat alternatives: also a skeptic

- Big question: who's the target audience? Who's going to get on board with cultured meat who isn't already on board with Impossible meat? Can you actually picture her in your mind? How big an audience is this?
- The meat alternatives industry is really struggling (Beyond Meat down \~97% from peak valuation). What's up with that?
- My belief, and I hope to persuade you about this: the inability of plant-based meats to find their foothold tells you something important about the cultured meat market.
- Survey data suggests a *lot* of resistance ([Peacock 2026](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0195666325004544)).

## Corporate/legal campaigns: I'm fine with "part of the solution"

- Cage-free commitments, BCC, gestation crates, etc.
- But ofc companies can reneg, laws can be overturned
- A lot of these campaigns are [aligned with public opinion](https://www.vox.com/future-perfect/488861/meat-paradox-factory-farming-animals?view_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpZCI6InlnRldSSXAwVk0iLCJwIjoiL2Z1dHVyZS1wZXJmZWN0LzQ4ODg2MS9tZWF0LXBhcmFkb3gtZmFjdG9yeS1mYXJtaW5nLWFuaW1hbHMiLCJleHAiOjE3ODAzMjM2MjksImlhdCI6MTc3OTExNDAyOX0.ABZI3Db-3dA5FSFs2Xt9SauGz88fuHRF_r7OOTxcUss&utm_medium=gift-link), but not with a meaningful voting bloc. Americans oppose gestation crates but obviously DGAF about Save our Bacon Act – not enough to mobilize anyway.
- IMHO there's no path forward without convincing people that factory farming is not just *bad* but unacceptable. Right now we're at "bad, but I don't really care."

## So where does that leave us?

- Defaults, alt proteins, corporate campaigns replaced individual persuasion
- I don't see a vegan world emerging from any of these
- Best case: less cruel factory farming in 50 years
- But I want something more transformational!!

## Let's get weirder

> Paul Graham, [*Black Swan Farming*](https://paulgraham.com/swan.html)*:* "The best ideas look initially like bad ideas...If a good idea were obviously good, someone else would already have done it."

- Context here is startup ideas that change the world but that seemed insane at the outset, like a business that hinges on letting strangers into your home days/weeks at a time.

- Likewise,defaults, alt proteins, and campaigns allI sound like good ideas. I want to hear more ideas that are like Airbnb or Dropbox, something that will probably fail but might work in a huge way

## Maybe that means literally weird as in "WTH??"

::::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth, height=0.65\textheight, keepaspectratio]{images/fish-sauce-serving-spoon.png}
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
- [Thai study](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0238642): put a hole in the fish sauce spoon. Make it inconvenient to do your normal stuff
- I think this would never fly in America but who cares? If it works there, great
- Small reduction in fish sauce per person (\textasciitilde{}0.58g per bowl; [Kanchanachitra et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0238642)), but fish sauce fishes are really small so that's actually a lot of fish lives
:::
:::::

## Or really not scalable or without any clear application

- You know one cafeteria, one community really well and your idea would only work there
  - "I can't scale this, so why bother?" No!! Let's all do something that works and let's record a lot of qualitative results so we can [build some theory](https://regressiontothemeat.substack.com/p/moralization-even-with-clear-cut)
- Or you might have an idea where you can't see a way any advocacy group would take up the mantle
  - Fine with me. Ex: I want to talk to people about fear, and early childhood, and food. One on one, really listening. I can't see any way someone would take that baton from me. But it's interesting and it might generate insights and that's fine ("*Do not trouble your hearts overmuch with thought of the road tonight").*

- Especially if you want to test them rigorously & want someone to do the IRB paperwork & coauthor the paper, I'm here for it ([setgree\@stanford.edu](mailto:setgree@stanford.edu))
